$comment: Seirin cast — OPEN QUESTIONS, not answers. This file records what the design document actually fixes (name, age, role, faction) and then asks the questions whose answers become the character's visual design. Answers are supplied by the project owner or a design agent, NOT by the art agent. Until a question is answered its value stays null. See ../SKILL.md and ../references/wardrobe-questions.md.
status: UNANSWERED — no character below has an approved visual design yet.

how_to_use.1: Read the question set in question_template. It applies to every character.
how_to_use.2: Answer per character, in this file, replacing null. Short answers are fine.
how_to_use.3: An answer is only 'canon' once the project owner approves it. Mark approved:true.
how_to_use.4: The art agent may NOT invent answers. If a field is null, it asks.

note_on_canon: The existing design document is a draft and is itself AI-generated. Treat it as a starting point to interrogate, not as canon. Where it conflicts with a better answer, the better answer wins — record the change.

silhouette: What shape is this person from 50 metres away, in one word?
Could you tell them from every other cast member as a black shape? What makes that true?
wardrobe: What does this person actually wear on an ordinary working day, given their job?
Where do their clothes come from — inherited, issued, bought cheap, made, stolen?
What do they wear when it rains? When it is cold? Seirin is a coastal city with real weather.
Do they own more than one outfit? Which ones, and when does each get worn?
What is worn out, repaired, stained or too big? What does that say about their life?
Whose clothes are these really — do they fit, and were they chosen by this person?
wardrobe_sources: Which real garment tradition does this draw on? (See references/wardrobe-questions.md for the catalogue.)
Why would THIS person, in THIS city, plausibly own it?
What is the fastening, the layering, the weight of the cloth? Real clothes have construction.
If the answer is 'a bodysuit' or 'sci-fi armour' — why? Is that a decision or a default?
identity: What is the one detail someone describes when telling a friend about them?
What second detail is only noticed the second time you look?
Which of these details exists BECAUSE of who they are, rather than as decoration?
face_and_body: What face should this character have, and what does that face communicate before they speak?
What are the eyes doing when the character is not being addressed?
What body does this person's actual life give them — their work, age, health, habits?
colour: What three colours, and why those?
Which single colour is reserved so it means something when it appears?
Do they read as themselves in the rain, at night, in a lit interior?
expression: What is their neutral, resting face — the one seen most often?
What is the difference between their public face and their private one?
boundaries: What must this character NEVER look like, and why is that a risk worth naming?
Which visual cliché is this character most likely to collapse into if nobody resists it?
